key_insight: Pangram 4 is a highly accurate AI-text classifier that improves on Pangram 3, with strong resistance to out-of-distribution inputs and adversarial manipulation. It can better tell apart subtle edits and mixed AI-human text, making detection more reliable in real-world use.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately detecting AI-generated text while remaining robust to edited, mixed, and adversarially altered content.
method: Uses a deep-learning-based text classification model trained for AI-text detection.
Evaluates performance with AUROC, false positive rate, and false negative rate.
Tests robustness on out-of-distribution samples and adversarial attacks, including fine-grained edits and mixed AI-human text.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Pangram 4 offers a more dependable tool for content verification and model auditing. Its robustness makes it especially useful in settings where text may be edited, combined, or intentionally manipulated to evade detection.
visual_elements: A performance dashboard showing AUROC, false positive rate, and false negative rate.
A comparison bar chart of Pangram 3 vs. Pangram 4 accuracy and robustness.
A robustness flow diagram illustrating clean text, edited text, mixed text, and adversarial attacks.
An icon-based pipeline showing input text -> classifier -> AI vs human label.
paper_authors: Ben Glickenhaus, Katherine Thai, Jenna Russell, Elyas Masrour, Yue Han
